subtopics.name: Discharge planning and continuity of care

questions.stem: The nurse on a labor and delivery unit receives report on four clients. Which client should the nurse see first?

options.text: A client at 39 weeks, 4 cm dilated, contracting every 4 minutes, who is asking for an epidural
A client at 32 weeks with sudden severe abdominal pain, a rigid uterus and dark vaginal bleeding
A client at 38 weeks whose membranes ruptured with clear fluid; fetal heart rate 140 with moderate variability
A client at 36 weeks with a blood pressure of 148/94 and a mild headache eased by acetaminophen

rationale.correct: Placental abruption threatens both lives and needs immediate action; stable labor and mild hypertension without severe features can follow.

perOption.a: She needs attention soon, but she and the fetus are stable.
perOption.b: These findings suggest placental abruption, an emergency for both the client and the fetus.
perOption.c: Clear fluid and a reassuring fetal heart rate are stable findings.
perOption.d: This may be preeclampsia and needs assessment soon, but there are no severe features and it is less urgent than an abruption.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The RN on a postpartum unit is working with an LPN and assistive personnel. For each task, choose the staff member the RN should assign it to.

rows.text: First assessment of a client just transferred from labor and delivery
Giving scheduled oral ibuprofen to a stable client
Helping a client walk to the bathroom for the first time after birth
Weighing a stable newborn at the scheduled time

rationale.correct: Match each task to the most limited scope that can do it safely, and keep first-time activities after birth with the RN.

perOption.r1:c1: The initial assessment is an RN responsibility.
perOption.r1:c2: LPNs do not do initial assessments.
perOption.r2:c1: The RN could, but this is within LPN scope.
perOption.r2:c2: Giving oral medications to a stable client is within LPN scope.
perOption.r3:c1: The first time out of bed after birth needs RN assessment because of fainting and bleeding risk.
perOption.r3:c2: The RN should assess the first walk.
perOption.r3:c3: Later walks can be delegated once the client is stable.
perOption.r4:c1: The RN could, but it is best delegated.
perOption.r4:c2: The LPN could, but it is best delegated.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse on a pediatric unit receives four updates at the start of the shift. Which child should the nurse see first?

options.text: A 3-year-old with a new arm cast who is crying for a parent; the fingers are pink and warm
A 6-month-old with bronchiolitis whose respiratory rate rose from 48 to 72/min with nasal flaring
A 10-year-old with type 1 diabetes whose glucose is 72 mg/dL and who wants a snack before gym class
A 14-year-old 1 day after an appendectomy whose pain is 3 out of 10 after oral medication

rationale.correct: Infants decompensate quickly, so increasing respiratory distress comes first.

perOption.a: Good circulation in the fingers is reassuring; the emotional need can be met after urgent problems.
perOption.b: Increasing work of breathing in an infant can progress quickly to respiratory failure.
perOption.c: A glucose at the low end of normal needs a snack soon, which can be arranged quickly.
perOption.d: Pain is controlled.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The RN on a pediatric unit is planning care with assistive personnel (AP). Which task can the RN delegate to the AP?

options.text: Measuring and recording the intake and output of a stable child
Teaching a parent how to give an inhaler through a spacer
Reassessing a child's pain 30 minutes after IV morphine
Giving a child the scheduled dose of oral amoxicillin

rationale.correct: AP can measure and record for stable children; RNs assess, evaluate and teach.

perOption.a: Routine measurement for a stable child can be delegated.
perOption.b: Teaching is an RN responsibility.
perOption.c: Evaluating the response to an opioid is an RN responsibility.
perOption.d: AP do not give medications.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse on an inpatient mental health unit hears raised voices in the day room. Which situation needs the nurse's immediate attention?

options.text: A client with depression who skipped group therapy and is resting in their room
A client who is shouting at another client and lifting a chair overhead
A client with schizophrenia who is quietly talking to unseen voices in a corner
A client pacing the hallway and asking for the PRN anxiety medication

rationale.correct: Imminent harm to self or others comes first on a mental health unit.

perOption.a: This needs follow-up today but there is no immediate danger.
perOption.b: Imminent violence threatens the safety of both clients and staff.
perOption.c: This needs monitoring, but there is no immediate danger.
perOption.d: This client needs attention soon, but the risk is lower than imminent violence.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize safety on a mental health unit.

questions.stem: A client with bipolar disorder who is stable on lithium is ready for discharge from a mental health unit but has no housing. Which action best supports continuity of care?

options.text: Give the client a printed list of local shelters on the day of discharge
Work with the social worker on housing and book follow-up before discharge
Keep the client on the unit until a permanent apartment becomes available
Ask the client to find housing first and then call to book follow-up

rationale.correct: Mental health discharge planning addresses social needs such as housing and arranges follow-up before the client leaves.

perOption.a: A list alone gives too little support for a safe transition.
perOption.b: Transition planning that covers housing and follow-up reduces relapse and readmission.
perOption.c: Staying in hospital once the client is stable is not appropriate.
perOption.d: This leaves the client without support at a vulnerable time.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse on an oncology unit is reviewing updates on six clients at the start of the shift. Highlight the client situations that need the nurse's attention first.

cells: Receiving chemotherapy; nausea controlled with a scheduled antiemetic
Hair loss; asking about a wig
Lung cancer; new facial swelling and distended neck veins
Leukemia; platelets 8,000/mm3 and a new nosebleed

rationale.correct: Oncology emergencies include neutropenic fever, superior vena cava syndrome and severe bleeding with very low platelets.

perOption.r2: Neutropenic fever is an emergency; cultures and antibiotics are needed within an hour.
perOption.r3: Emotional support is needed, but it is not urgent.
perOption.r4: These findings suggest superior vena cava syndrome.
perOption.r6: There is a high risk of serious bleeding.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The triage nurse in the emergency department is sorting three new arrivals. For each client, select the most appropriate triage level.

cells.text: Client with chest pain who is sweating, with a blood pressure of 88/50
Client with a possible forearm fracture, a radial pulse present and pain of 6 out of 10
Client with a sore throat for 2 days who has no fever and normal vital signs

options.text: Emergent (immediate)
Urgent
Non-urgent
Emergent (immediate)
Urgent
Non-urgent
Emergent (immediate)
Urgent
Non-urgent

rationale.correct: Triage sorts clients by how quickly they need care: threats to life first, then threats to limb or function, then minor problems.

perOption.b1:a: This client needs life-saving intervention now.
perOption.b1:b: This is too low for signs of shock.
perOption.b2:b: The client needs imaging and pain control soon but is stable.
perOption.b2:c: The client needs imaging and pain control within hours.
perOption.b3:a: There is no threat to life.
perOption.b3:b: There is no threat to life or limb.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The charge nurse in the intensive care unit is making assignments. Which client is most appropriate for a nurse who finished ICU orientation last week?

options.text: A client on a ventilator for 4 days with stable settings and vital signs
A client with an intra-aortic balloon pump whose hemodynamics are changing
A client in septic shock whose three vasopressors are being titrated
A client who arrived from the operating room after cardiac surgery an hour ago

rationale.correct: Match a client's stability and complexity to the nurse's experience.

perOption.a: Stable but complex care suits a newly oriented nurse, with experienced help nearby.
perOption.b: This client is unstable and needs advanced skills.
perOption.c: This client is unstable and needs an experienced ICU nurse.
perOption.d: A fresh post-cardiac surgery client needs an experienced nurse.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old client newly diagnosed with heart failure is going home after 4 days in hospital. Which items belong in the discharge plan? Select all that apply.

options.text: A follow-up appointment within 7 days of discharge
Daily weights, with instructions on when to call the provider
A reconciled medication list given to the client
Teaching about a sodium-restricted diet
A referral to cardiac rehabilitation or home health as needed
Instructions to stop the diuretic once the swelling goes down
Advice to drink extra fluids to protect the kidneys

rationale.correct: Heart failure discharge plans include early follow-up, daily weights, medications, diet and referrals.

perOption.a: Early follow-up reduces readmissions.
perOption.b: Weight gain is an early sign of fluid overload.
perOption.c: This prevents medication errors.
perOption.d: Limiting sodium helps prevent fluid retention.
perOption.f: Stopping a diuretic without the provider is unsafe.
perOption.g: Clients with heart failure often need to limit fluids.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client being discharged after a hip fracture repair says, "I don't have a car and I can't afford taxis to get to my physical therapy and surgeon visits." What should the nurse do?

options.text: Suggest the client ask a neighbor or friend to drive them to the visits each week
Refer the client to the social worker or case manager for transport
Ask the surgeon whether the follow-up visits could be skipped
Document that the client is unlikely to follow the discharge plan

rationale.correct: Identify and address barriers to follow-up, such as transport, before discharge.

perOption.a: This may not be reliable, and it does not use available resources.
perOption.b: These team members can arrange transport resources and address the barrier.
perOption.c: Missing follow-up after hip surgery is unsafe.
perOption.d: The problem is a barrier to care, not unwillingness.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client who spent 5 days in the ICU with sepsis is being transferred to a medical unit. Which information is most important for the ICU nurse to include in the handoff?

options.text: Recent changes in condition, pending tests and what to watch for next
The medications given during the ICU stay, listed out one day at a time
The family's contact details and their preferred visiting times
The ICU nurse's impression of how the family has been coping

rationale.correct: Transfer handoffs focus on current status, recent changes, pending results and risks.

perOption.a: This lets the receiving nurse continue care safely and spot early deterioration.
perOption.b: Current medications matter, but a full day-by-day history is less useful than current risks.
perOption.c: This is useful but is not the priority for safe care.
perOption.d: This may help later, but it is not the most important information.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client recovering from a stroke coughs when drinking thin liquids, cannot walk safely without help, and is worried about paying the rent while off work. For each need, select the team member who should be involved.

options.text: Speech-language pathologist
Occupational therapist
Physical therapist
Occupational therapist
Social worker
Chaplain

rationale.correct: Interprofessional referrals should match each of the client's needs.

perOption.a: The SLP evaluates and treats dysphagia.
perOption.b: OT helps with self-feeding, not the swallow itself.
perOption.c: PT improves mobility and gait.
perOption.d: OT focuses on daily activities rather than gait training.
perOption.e: The social worker helps with financial resources.
perOption.f: The chaplain gives spiritual support, not financial help.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client admitted with abdominal pain asks the nurse, "Why is my doctor ordering so many tests? Nobody has told me what they're looking for." What should the nurse do?

options.text: Tell the client not to worry, since the tests are routine
Share what is known and ask the provider to explain
Tell the client the doctor is probably being overly careful
Offer to cancel any tests the client doesn't want

rationale.correct: Nurses help clients get information about their care from the provider.

perOption.a: This dismisses the question.
perOption.b: This supports the client's right to information about their care.
perOption.c: This undermines the provider without facts.
perOption.d: Canceling tests is not within the nurse's role.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A medical unit has had six medication errors during the 0900 medication pass this quarter. Most happened when nurses were interrupted. Which change is most likely to reduce these errors?

options.text: A no-interruption zone and vest while nurses prepare medications
Having nurses prepare the 0900 medications at 0500 before clients wake
A second-nurse check for every oral medication on the unit
Posting a list of recent errors on the medication room door

rationale.correct: Reducing interruptions during medication preparation is an effective system-level safety strategy.

perOption.a: Interruptions are a leading cause of medication errors, so protecting preparation time targets the cause.
perOption.b: Preparing medications hours early increases mix-ups.
perOption.c: This adds workload without addressing interruptions.
perOption.d: Warnings are a weak strategy that does not remove the cause.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse on a surgical unit receives four reports at once. Place the clients in the order the nurse should see them, from first to last.

items.text: A client 2 hours after surgery whose SpO2 has just fallen to 84%
A client with pain of 8 out of 10 whose next dose is due now
A client with sudden heavy bleeding through the dressing and a heart rate of 120/min
A client asking what time discharge will be tomorrow

rationale.correct: Airway and breathing, then circulation, then comfort, then routine questions.

perOption.a: Hypoxemia is the most immediate threat.
perOption.b: Hemorrhage comes next, as a circulation threat.
perOption.c: Pain is important but not life-threatening.
perOption.d: This is not urgent.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The RN on a medical unit is planning the morning with assistive personnel (AP). Select the 3 tasks the RN can delegate to the AP.

options.text: Changing the bed linen of a stable client
Taking vital signs on a stable client
Helping a stable client with no swallowing problems eat lunch
Assessing a newly found wound on the heel
Teaching a client about a newly prescribed medication
Evaluating a client's response to pain medication

rationale.correct: AP can give routine care to stable clients; assessment, teaching and evaluation stay with the RN.

perOption.a: This is routine care.
perOption.b: This is routine for a stable client.
perOption.c: This is routine when there is no swallowing problem.
perOption.d: Assessment is RN work.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse has 15 minutes before a required staff meeting and time for only one task. Which task should the nurse do first?

options.text: Give a time-critical IV antibiotic that is now 30 minutes late
Document the morning assessments for two stable clients
Return a family member's call about visiting hours
Update the care plan for a client who is going home tomorrow morning

rationale.correct: Time-critical care comes before documentation and routine tasks.

perOption.a: Time-critical medications must not be delayed beyond their window.
perOption.b: Charting can be completed after the meeting.
perOption.c: This can wait or be passed to the unit clerk.
perOption.d: This can be done later in the shift.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Manage time on a busy shift.

questions.stem: The nurse on a renal unit receives report on four clients. Which client should the nurse see first?

options.text: A client with CKD who missed dialysis; potassium 6.9 mEq/L and weak legs
A client with a urinary tract infection who reports burning on urination
A client with a kidney stone whose pain is 6 out of 10, 30 minutes after IV morphine
A client with benign prostatic hyperplasia who voided 300 mL with a residual of 80 mL

rationale.correct: Life-threatening electrolyte levels with symptoms are the priority.

perOption.a: Severe hyperkalemia with muscle weakness can cause a fatal dysrhythmia.
perOption.b: This is expected with the infection and is not urgent.
perOption.c: The pain is improving and can be reassessed shortly.
perOption.d: This residual is acceptable.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The RN asked assistive personnel to walk a client in the hallway. The AP returns and says the client became dizzy and pale on standing, so the AP helped the client back to bed. What should the RN do?

options.text: Ask the AP to try the walk again in an hour, once the client has rested
Assess the client, including lying and standing vital signs
Document that the client declined to walk this morning
Ask the AP to walk the client with a gait belt and a wheelchair behind

rationale.correct: New symptoms reported by AP need the RN's own assessment before care continues.

perOption.a: A new symptom needs RN assessment before another attempt.
perOption.b: New dizziness on standing needs RN assessment for orthostatic hypotension and other causes.
perOption.c: This would be inaccurate documentation.
perOption.d: Extra equipment does not replace assessment of the new symptom.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A nurse educator is teaching new graduates how to set priorities at the start of a shift on a medical-surgical unit with six clients. Complete the sentence.

content.template: When setting priorities, the nurse should first address {{b1}}, and should see {{b2}} before stable clients with expected findings.

options.text: airway, breathing and circulation
each client's stated preferences
documentation that is overdue
clients with new or unexpected changes
clients who are going home today
clients who are still asleep

rationale.correct: Use the ABCs first, then look for acute, unexpected changes.

perOption.b1:b: Preferences matter, but they do not come first.
perOption.b2:b: Clients being discharged are usually stable.
perOption.b2:c: Being asleep is not a priority factor.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: Using Maslow's hierarchy of needs, which client need should the nurse meet first?

options.text: A client who feels lonely and wants company
A client who is dehydrated and dizzy
A client who wants to learn about the illness
A client worried about a new surgical scar

rationale.correct: Physiological needs come before safety, belonging and esteem.

perOption.a: Belonging needs come after physiological needs.
perOption.b: Physiological needs come first.
perOption.c: Learning needs come later.
perOption.d: Esteem needs come later.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client with vertebral osteomyelitis has a PICC line and needs IV antibiotics every 12 hours for 6 more weeks. The client wants to go home and has a supportive partner. Which referral is most appropriate?

options.text: Home infusion services with home health nursing
Transfer to a skilled nursing facility for the 6 weeks
Outpatient physical therapy for back strengthening
A dietitian consult to support bone healing

rationale.correct: Home infusion services support long-term IV therapy at home when the client is able.

perOption.a: These services allow safe IV therapy and line care at home.
perOption.b: This is more restrictive than needed for a client with support at home.
perOption.c: Therapy may help later, but it does not provide the antibiotics.
perOption.d: Nutrition matters, but it is not the main need.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse on a medical unit receives report on four clients with gastrointestinal problems. Which client should the nurse assess first?

options.text: A client with cirrhosis and mild ascites who is asking for a snack
A client with a nasogastric tube to suction draining green fluid
A client with an upper GI bleed who is newly anxious; HR 124, BP 90/58
A client with constipation for 3 days who is asking for a laxative

rationale.correct: Signs of shock from hemorrhage are a priority; new anxiety can be an early sign.

perOption.a: This client is stable.
perOption.b: Green bile-colored drainage is expected.
perOption.c: New anxiety with tachycardia and falling pressure are signs of hypovolemic shock from bleeding.
perOption.d: This is not urgent.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize a client with GI bleeding.

questions.stem: The nurse is calling the on-call provider at night about a client whose blood pressure has fallen. Which statement is the best way to open the call?

options.text: "I'm worried about Mr. Smith in room 12. Can you come and see him?"
"This is Ana, Mr. Smith's nurse in 12. His BP fell to 84/50 this hour."
"Mr. Smith's labs are back, and I have some questions about them."
"Mr. Smith had a bowel resection 2 days ago and also has type 2 diabetes."

rationale.correct: Start SBAR with who you are, who the client is and what the problem is.

perOption.a: This shows concern but does not say what the problem is.
perOption.b: The SBAR situation identifies the caller and the client and states the problem first.
perOption.c: This is vague and does not state the urgent problem.
perOption.d: This is background, which follows the situation in SBAR.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse is reviewing messages from assistive personnel and clients on a medical-surgical unit. For each finding, choose whether it requires immediate action or can be addressed later.

rows.text: New confusion in a client 1 day after surgery
A client asking about visiting hours
A client with a new heart rate of 40/min who feels dizzy
A client asking for extra pillows
A client with chest pain rated 7 out of 10

rationale.correct: Acute changes need immediate action; comfort and information requests can wait or be delegated.

perOption.r1:c1: This may signal hypoxia, bleeding or infection.
perOption.r4:c2: It can be delegated or addressed later.
perOption.r5:c1: This may be acute coronary syndrome.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The RN is assigning work to an LPN on a medical unit at the start of the day shift. Which instruction to the LPN is most appropriate?

options.text: "Check on room 5 when you get a chance and do whatever she needs."
"Give the 1000 meds in 3 and 4; tell me if a systolic is under 100."
"Please do the admission assessment for the new client in room 8."
"Please write up the nursing care plan for the client in room 6."

rationale.correct: Clear assignment states the task, the time, the limits and what to report.

perOption.a: This is too vague to be safe.
perOption.b: This states the task, the time and exactly what to report.
perOption.c: The initial assessment is an RN responsibility.
perOption.d: Care planning is an RN responsibility.
